chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ribʿī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Jārūd, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

When booty came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, he would take its choicest part, and that belonged to him. Then he would divide what remained into five fifths, then take its khums, then divide the four fifths among the people. Then he would divide the khums that he had taken into five fifths: he would take the share of Allah for himself, then divide the four fifths among the near relatives, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer; and he mentioned the hadith to its end.

So this does not contradict the first report stating that the khums is divided into six shares, because it only contains an account of the action of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and that he عليه السلام only used to take from the khums the share of Allah and his own share, and these are two shares out of six. It is possible that he was content in that regard with the khums so that the remainder might be left in full for the other deserving recipients. There is nothing in the report stating that this is a binding rule in every circumstance such that مخالفة of it is impermissible; rather, it is only an account of his action عليه السلام, and that does not conflict with what the first report indicated regarding the obligation of dividing the khums into six shares. We have fully discussed what relates to this chapter in our larger book, so whoever wants it may find it there.

key_terms.ابْنِ السَّبِيلِ: the stranded traveler entitled to support
key_terms.الْخُمُسَ: the one-fifth tax taken from the spoils
key_terms.الْمَغْنَمُ: war booty or spoils acquired in battle
key_terms.ذَوِي الْقُرْبَى: the near relatives entitled to a designated share
key_terms.صَفْوَهُ: the choicest selected portion taken before general distribution

ai.seo_question: How was khums divided by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم according to al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This report describes how the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم dealt with war booty and the division of khums, including his taking the selected portion and distributing the remaining shares among the designated recipients. The accompanying discussion explains that this practical example does not negate other reports establishing six shares for khums, because it is treated as a narration of the Prophet’s action rather than an absolute legal formula in every case.
